title: Glossopharyngeal Nerve Chronic Recording In Anesthetized Rat
author: Grant A McCallum
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wssfeee

steps.title: Sterilize instruments and implants
steps.instruction: Autoclave all surgical instruments and implant assemblies at 250 °C for 1 hour before beginning the surgery.

steps.title: Administer local and systemic analgesia
steps.instruction: Inject lidocaine (4 mg/kg) plus bupivacaine (2 mg/kg) subcutaneously at the surgical site at least 30 seconds before incision, and inject carprofen (5 mg/kg) subcutaneously at the time of surgery; repeat carprofen once daily for the next 4 days.

steps.title: Induce and maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the rat under gas anesthesia with 2 % isoflurane delivered in 1 L/min oxygen (or alternatively ketamine/xylazine) for the duration of the procedure.

steps.title: Expose and isolate glossopharyngeal nerve
steps.instruction: Perform a surgical exposure of the glossopharyngeal nerve; isolate a 3–4 mm segment free of connective tissue and suspend it using a custom hook mounted on a three‑axis micromanipulator.

substeps.instruction: Remove the slip knot to release the silicone tube junction from the microneedle.

steps.title: Implant CNT yarn electrodes
steps.instruction: Advance the CNT‑yarn electrode assembly into the nerve until the uninsulated CNT segment lies within the perineurium, apply gentle pressure with micro‑tweezers, and carefully withdraw the tungsten microneedle, leaving the CNT yarn in place.

substeps.instruction: Move the hook ~2 mm along the nerve to the next site and repeat the implantation process.
After completing all implant sites, position the CNT yarns and silicone tube junctions within the incision.

steps.title: Seal implant site with fibrin glue
steps.instruction: Apply 1 mL of fibrin glue (Tisseel, Baxter International Inc.) to completely encapsulate the CNT yarns and silicone tube junctions, allowing natural collagen encapsulation as the glue is absorbed.

steps.title: Route wires to percutaneous plug
steps.instruction: Tunnel the free DFT® wire ends to a location on the back between the shoulder blades, externalize them, pass them through a custom percutaneous silicone plug, and solder them to an MCP‑05‑SS Omnetics connector.

substeps.instruction: Fit the connector inside the silicone tube of the plug and fill the tube with UV‑curable medical‑grade epoxy (OG603).

steps.title: Create pocket and close incisions
steps.instruction: Perform blunt dissection to create a sub‑cutaneous pocket between skin and muscle on the back, place the implanted wires and ground wire inside, and suture the plug’s mesh base to the underlying muscle fascia with biodegradable 3‑0 Vicryl Plus sutures.

substeps.instruction: Close all skin incision sites using 4‑0 Webpro™ sutures.

steps.title: Configure neural acquisition system
steps.instruction: Connect the percutaneous plug to the custom PCBs (MCS‑05‑DD and NPD‑36‑AA‑GS Omnetics connectors) and to the Intan RHD2216 neural amplifier board; set the acquisition system (Intan C3100/RHD20000) to 20 k samples/sec per amplifier, enable DSP offset removal, set high‑pass filter at 100 Hz, band‑pass filter between 100 Hz and 9 kHz, and configure the trigger input to sample at 20 k samples/sec.

substeps.instruction: Record a manual trigger signal via a push‑button switch to mark experimental events.

steps.title: Perform hypoxia challenge series
steps.instruction: Lightly sedate the rat with isoflurane or ketamine/xylazine, measure electrode impedance via the port, and begin neural recordings; then expose the animal to a gas mixture of 10 % O₂ and 90 % N₂ at 1 L/min flow until oxygen saturation drops to 70 % (≈30 seconds).

substeps.instruction: Allow a 5‑minute recovery interval before the next challenge.
Repeat the hypoxia exposure three times per session.
Conduct one hypoxia session per week for 6 weeks.
